turnaround_reason: Charter (Spectrum) has been derated toward multi-year lows as broadband subscriber losses accelerated (-172k in Q2 2026) amid fixed-wireless and fiber competition, producing a fourth consecutive quarterly revenue decline against a heavy debt load. The bull case is deep value: massive free cash flow, growing mobile (12M lines), shrinking video losses, and the just-closed $34.5B Cox merger with $800M of targeted synergies.
bullish_points: Very large insider buying: net +1.58M shares over 6 months across 22 purchase transactions — a strong bottom-fishing signal
Substantial free cash flow (~$2.2B) supports deleveraging and buybacks even amid revenue declines
Cox merger (closed, $34.5B) adds scale with ~$800M of identified synergies
Mobile is a real growth engine (~12M lines) and video subscriber losses are shrinking sharply
Deeply depressed valuation: ~47% of the 200-week MA and ~19% below the 200-day, with improving 30-day momentum (+13%)
bearish_points: Enormous leverage: ~$96.7B total debt (EV ~$119B vs ~$20B equity) in a higher-for-longer rate environment
Core broadband is in secular decline: fixed wireless (T-Mobile, Verizon) and fiber structurally erode the subscriber base
Four consecutive quarters of revenue decline; the top line has not yet stabilized
Merger integration risk and California-imposed investment conditions add near-term cost
A levered equity stub means small changes in EBITDA/rates swing the equity value hard
catalyst: Cox synergy realization plus broadband sub-loss stabilization and continued mobile growth translating into FCF/equity de-risking
catalyst_timing: Next 2-3 quarters (2H 2026 into 2027) as merger integration and network upgrades progress
suggested_trade: Starter spot position for deep-value/insider-buying exposure; longer-dated LEAPS an option given liquid chain
key_risk: Fixed-wireless/fiber keep structurally shrinking broadband while the ~$97B debt load caps equity upside and amplifies downside
would_skip_if: Broadband net losses keep accelerating with no stabilization, or merger synergies slip and leverage metrics deteriorate
